name: Signal Strength Estimation and Classification in High-Energy Physics Data
description: Develop machine learning models to estimate the signal strength parameter (µ) and classify particle collision events as Signal or Background, while accounting for systematic and random uncertainties.

cr:input.name: competition_dataset
cr:input.description: The input data consists of tabular features derived from proton-proton collision events at the LHC. Features include raw measurements (e.g., energy, momentum, transverse momentum, azimuthal angle, pseudorapidity, missing transverse energy) and derived quantities (e.g., transverse mass, invariant mass, pseudorapidity separations). Labels include binary classification (Signal or Background) and detailed event types (e.g., htautau, ztautau). Systematic biases are introduced via nuisance parameters simulating detector miscalibration and background shifts.

cr:output.name: predictions
cr:output.description: The output should include the 68.27% confidence interval for the signal strength parameter µ, represented by its lower (mu_16) and upper (mu_84) bounds, as well as binary classification labels (1 for Signal, 0 for Background). µ values range from 0.1 to 3, and classification labels are integers (0 or 1).

field.name: id
field.description: unique identifier for the collision event, e.g., event_001

field.name: mu_16
field.description: lower bound of the 68.27% confidence interval for µ

field.name: mu_84
field.description: upper bound of the 68.27% confidence interval for µ

field.name: classification
field.description: binary classification label: 1 for Signal, 0 for Background

cr:evaluation.notes: The Final Quantile Score is computed as -ln((w + ε)f(c)), where ε = 10^-2 and f(c) penalizes deviations from 68.27% coverage asymmetrically. Smaller interval widths (w) and accurate coverage (c) improve the score.
